contexts.text: Rings and nose jewels () = good and its badges.

And Pharaoh removed his ring from upon his hand () = what is confirmative concerning power which he before had... A ring = what is confirmative... Hence he removed his ring from upon his hand = that he abdicated the power he before had. (See Betroth here.)
To put a ring upon the hand of another = a confirmative that he yields to the other the power which was his.
Thou shalt cast for it [the ark] four rings of gold () = Divine Truth conjoined with Divine Good, which is everywhere round about. Rings = the conjunction of good and truth.
Two rings upon the one side of it, and two rings upon the other side of it () = the marriage of truth with good, and of good with truth... Rings = the conjunction or marriage of good with truth.
The rings = the conjunction itself... The staves have reference to the arms with man; the rings to the ball and socket joints where the arms are conjoined with the breast.

Thou shalt put the staves into the rings () = the power of the Divine sphere... The rings = Divine truth conjoined with Divine good, which is on every side round about; thus the Divine sphere which encompasses and closes in Heaven in general, and the heavenly societies and the Angels themselves in particular.
The staves must be in the rings of the ark () = that power is steadfast from the Divine sphere of good and truth.

Thou shalt make for it [the table] four rings of gold () = the ultimate receptacle of the heavenly marriage, which is that of Divine good with Divine truth. Four rings of gold = Divine truth conjoined with Divine good, which is everywhere round about; thus the ultimate receptacle of the heavenly marriage, which is that of Divine good with Divine truth. AC 9539.
Thou shalt put the rings upon its four corners () = stability... from the conjunction of Divine truth with Divine good in ultimates.
The boards shall be twinned below to one ring () = thus consistence or steadfastness. A ring = conjunction; here, steadfastness through conjunction.

Thou shalt make upon the network four rings of brass () = the sphere of good through which there is conjunction... Rings = the sphere of Divine good and of Divine truth, through which there is conjunction.

Thou shalt make upon the breastplate two rings of gold () = the sphere of Divine good through which there is conjunction on the side of the higher Heaven... The two rings of gold = the sphere of Divine good through which there is conjunction.
Thou shalt set the two rings upon the two extremities of the breastplate () = the conjunction of the sphere of Divine good in the extremes of Heaven.

Thou shalt bind the breastplate from its rings to the rings of the ephod () = the conjunction and preservation of all things of Heaven through the sphere of Divine good in the externals of the Spiritual Kingdom.
Thou shalt make two rings of gold for it [the altar of incense] under the border () = the sphere of Divine good through which there is conjunction and preservation. Explained.
The bridegroom placed a golden ring on her finger...
The ring which was put on the hand of the prodigal son = the conjunction of truth and good in the internal man.
